text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE NEWS

- President Farooq Leghari, promising to hold elections on schedule on February 3, has said the government had decided to grant an estimated two million people in the country's semi-autonomous tribal areas full voting rights.

- The caretaker government is heading for a crash on all the four important fronts of public finances as half of the current financial year is coming to a close with red entries of heavy mark-up loans occupying more pages on the ledgers.
- Ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto said after meeting her husband Asif Ali Zardari in jail that she feared for his life.

- Pakistan Muslim League leader Nawaz Sharif warned the caretaker government that any bid to oust the mainstream leaders from politics in the name of accountability will be disastrous for the country and the people will not accept it.
- The caretaker government of Prime Minister Meraj Khalid has decided to terminate the services of about 5,000 employees of the National Bank of Pakistan.
THE NATION
- Leghari issued an ordinance to withdraw income tax exemption on the salary and allowances of the president.
- The government is expected to place before the Senate (upper house) a list of more than 1,400 people barred from travelling abroad.
- The Indian Sugar General Imports and Exports Corporation has won the tender for supply of 50,000 metric tonnes of sugar at a rate of $360 per ton to Pakistan.
- Private air companies including Schon Air, Edhi Foundation and Union Texas have been refused permission to fly ever since the caretaker government assumed responsibility.
DAWN
- Pakistan has expressed serious concern at an increase in India's supplementary defence budget and deployment of missiles on borders.
- The State (central) Bank of Pakistan told all banks and financial institutions to resume rescheduling of unpaid loans.
- Pakistan has held successful talks with the World Bank and International Monetary Fund to secure $360 million to improve its balance of payments, a spokesman of President Farooq Leghari said.
- President Leghari said the forthcoming elections would not be postponed on the pretext of holding a fresh census.
- Riyadh has protested to Islamabad against what it calls mounting illegal immigration of Pakistanis to Saudi Arabia.
- Indian spinners said at a meeting with their Pakistani counterparts in Bombay that they opposed the export of Indian cotton to Pakistan.

- The government has decided to terminate the pre-shipment inspection contracts of two Swiss companies to save costs, Petroleum and Natural Resources Minister Javed Jabbar said. More than 50 percent of import items have been excluded from pre-shipment inspection by the two companies -- Cotecna and SGS.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- Pakistani officials in Washington are expected to conclude their visit with additional financial commitments of about $650 million from the IMF and the World Bank.
- Pakistan has expressed surprise at the United States turning a blind eye to the supply of heavy water by China to India's unsafeguarded nuclear power plant at Tarapur.
- The pharmaceutical industry has suspended investment plans worth 1.5 billion rupees due to ill-managed fiscal policies and diminishing profitability.
- President Farooq Leghari will inaugurate a three-day conference of economists organised by the Pakistan Society of Development Economists next week.
FINANCIAL POST
- The Italian government has warned the State (central) Bank of Pakistan of an influx of fake Italian currency in Karachi.

- Securitisation managers of state-run Pakistan Telecommunication Co Ltd are expected to disburse close to $150 million out of a total of $200 million before Christmas with negotiations continuing on how the deal will be structured.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
